clue.text: They're always open for late arrivals

definitions.text: They're always open for late arrivals

parts.words: They're always open for late arrivals
parts.note: surface reading: shops or doors kept open for people who turn up after hours
setter's reading: 'late' means deceased, so the arrivals are the newly dead coming to be buried

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like 'after time' but means 'dead', as in 'the late Mr Smith'; the entrances to a burial ground welcome such arrivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The entrances of a burial ground let in funerals bringing the recently deceased, so they stand open for the dead.

clue.text: He bills me incorrectly to decorate

indicators.note: something done incorrectly is wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tradesman overcharges a customer for doing up their home.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to adorn or ornament something, a straightforward synonym of decorating it.

clue.text: Praise the boot rejected by lieutenant

indicators.note: in a down clue something rejected is sent back up, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: getting the boot and getting the axe both mean being sacked
LT is the standard abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer turns down praise and sacks someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to glorify or extol them, so it is a verb synonym of praise.

clue.text: Competition from the first female conservationists

parts.note: in Genesis Eve is the first woman
the National Trust is the British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: A contest organised by a pioneering woman among nature lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting event is a single contest or race within a larger meeting, such as an Olympic final.

clue.text: It's OK to dry tea blended 24 hours ago

parts.note: an answer of agreement, saying something is fine

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so these letters are stirred into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone approves of leaving tea leaves to dry after mixing them the day before.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today is exactly the span of a day back, so the phrase describes the adverb meaning on the previous day.

clue.text: Sinner sexually explicit before mid-afternoon

parts.note: adult films or material are sexually explicit
an old poetic word for before

indicators.note: mid- points to the central letter of the following word only

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters is the centre

explanation.surface: A racy afternoon encounter leaves someone feeling guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' is not just a position word here: it supplies the archaic ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who commits adultery breaks a commandment, so the sinner is a particular kind of wrongdoer by example.

clue.text: Excise on cycles, the first ever

parts.note: eras are long ages or periods, as cycles of history

indicators.note: the first takes only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A tax on bicycles, the first one ever levied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excise' looks like the duty on goods, but here it is the verb meaning to cut out. In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise text is to cut it out or delete it, which is what rubbing it out does.

clue.text: Leaves this off regularly?

parts.note: surface reading: someone habitually omits or forgets a thing
setter's reading: leaves are foliage, which this plant sheds every autumn

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for foliage, and 'off' is where the foliage ends up each year.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of this kind sheds all its foliage annually in autumn, unlike an evergreen.

clue.text: Gentle cleaner got fellow tea, thus erred badly

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A careful cleaner fetched a colleague some tea and so made a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumed duster on a stick flicks dust away lightly, so it is a soft-touch cleaning tool.

clue.text: Welcome half of them to stay

indicators.note: half of keeps just two of the four letters of the following word, here the back pair

parts.note: the second half of the word
a brace is a support or stay, as in a corset or building

explanation.surface: A host greets visitors and invites half of them to remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea is to accept it gladly, and as a noun a hug is a warm greeting.

clue.text: Said I'd missed handling banger

indicators.note: missed means left out, so the named letters are dropped from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
the letters to drop
the way something is handled or treated

explanation.surface: Someone admits they botched a firework or an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger is British slang for a sausage, as in bangers and mash; the surface pulls towards a firework or a clapped-out car.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday British slang a banger is a sausage, from the way it can burst when fried.

clue.text: Home needs permit for passage

parts.note: at home means in
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A householder applies for a licence to build a hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of the sea running inland forms a water channel or way through for boats.

clue.text: Management team working in river

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the following word

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

indicators.note: working means in operation, rearranged into a functioning order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Bosses get their staff to work out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The way a person or problem is handled or dealt with is its treatment, so it is a synonym for management.

clue.text: Applying for morning off when entertaining

indicators.note: off means removed, so the abbreviation for morning is taken away

parts.note: funny, diverting
a.m., ante meridiem, is before noon

explanation.surface: Someone requests a morning's leave to host guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a method or tool means putting it into practice, which is what applying it means.

clue.text: Fighter happy to rubbish excellent upbringing

parts.note: pleased

indicators.note: bringing something up in a down clue lifts it from bottom to top, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: nonsense
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A combatant is pleased to disparage someone's fine childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbringing' looks like a noun about childhood but splits as up-bringing, a reversal signal in a down clue covering both pieces before it. A1 is the old Lloyd's Register mark for first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators were armed men who fought in Roman arenas, so they are fighters by example.

clue.text: EEC trader upset timber supplier

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters fall into a new pattern

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A European Community merchant who sells wood is annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: This conifer yields fragrant wood prized for chests and pencils, so it provides lumber.

clue.text: NCO old, yet turned over a new leaf

indicators.note: turned over means churned around, so the letters come up in a different order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An ageing sergeant has nonetheless reformed his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over a new leaf' reads as the idiom for reforming, but splits into the indicator and a botanical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first seed leaf of a germinating plant, the earliest foliage a seedling puts out.

clue.text: Zorba, swimming in stream, finds bird

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the word for a stream

parts.note: a rill is a small brook

indicators.note: swimming means moving about freely, so the letters drift into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Zorba the Greek, bathing in a brook, spots a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a black-and-white auk of northern seas, named for its sharp-edged beak, so it is a seabird.

clue.text: A foreign well that's unwholesome

parts.note: un is French for a
in good health

explanation.surface: A water source abroad is contaminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a water source but is the adjective for being in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bad for body or mind, such as junk food or a sick habit, is harmful to wellbeing in both words.

clue.text: In Shiraz, Edwin got knocked down

indicators.note: In says the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A man named Edwin was flattened in an Iranian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Shiraz is a city in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that has been razed has been levelled or demolished, so it has been flattened to the ground.

clue.text: Relating to items noticed during oral examination?

definitions.text: Relating to items noticed during oral examination?

parts.words: Relating to items noticed during oral examination?
parts.note: surface reading: points that come up in a spoken test or viva
setter's reading: a doctor looking inside the mouth, where glands at the back of the throat are seen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral examination' suggests a viva, but here it is a doctor saying 'say ah' and peering at the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pertaining to the two lymph glands at the back of the throat that a doctor checks.

clue.text: Navy man stands in front here

definitions.note: the town itself is the place meant

indicators.note: in front says the man's piece comes ahead of the navy's letters
in a down clue someone who stands rises upright, so the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a common man's name
the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor stands at the front of the spot where we are.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'here' is a place: a town on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a Scottish town and former county, so 'here' points at a location in a loose cryptic way.

clue.text: Guru cheerfully removed a piece of decoration

indicators.note: removed means taken out of the words before it, where the letters are buried

parts.note: spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A holy teacher happily took away an ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gathered frill or pleated strip of fabric sewn on a garment as trimming.

clue.text: Is usual before obtaining capital

indicators.note: before places the second piece ahead of the first in the answer

parts.note: par is the normal or average level, as in 'up to par'
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is normal to get some money ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money, but it is the chief city of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The French seat of government is a national chief city, the main sense of capital here.

clue.text: Look up "King in pop music"

indicators.note: in puts the preceding letters inside the word for father

parts.note: pop and pa are both familiar names for father

indicators.note: up in a down clue sends the word upwards, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo means look, as in 'lo and behold'
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Search for a famous monarch of pop songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop music' reads as a genre, but 'pop' is dad and the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lively Bohemian dance and the tune written for it, so it is a kind of music.

clue.text: Thrown out of dubious dive, etc

indicators.note: dubious means shady and unreliable, so the letters cannot be trusted to stay in order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Customers are ejected from a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A dive is a disreputable bar or club, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants who are evicted are expelled from their home, forced out by a landlord or bailiff.

clue.text: Army officer to cover Eastern conflict

parts.note: COL is short for colonel
a lid covers a pot
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A colonel is sent to report on a war in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conflict' looks like a noun for war, but it is the verb: to clash.
explanation.definitionFit: When views or interests collide they clash and are at odds, which is to conflict as a verb.

clue.text: Lobbies Transport House with one point

parts.note: to transport someone is to delight or enrapture them
a hall is a large house, as in a manor
one point of the compass, south

explanation.surface: Pressure groups target the Labour Party's old headquarters to make a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport House was the Labour Party's London headquarters, so 'Lobbies' looks like a verb about politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobbies are foyers just inside a front door, so they are the rooms where visitors first come in.
